# BuildBrief

> BuildBrief turns an early-stage housing idea into a professional Development Intent Brief — the numbers, priorities, and pro-ready language that make architects, GCs, and lenders understand your project the first time.

BuildBrief is a free web tool at https://buildbrief.nesohq.com/. It runs in the browser with no account.
It is for first-time and small housing developers briefing an architect, contractor or lender.

## Questions BuildBrief answers

- **What does an architect need from me before schematic design starts?** A written statement of intent: the site, the unit or space program, the budget range, the schedule, the parking and access assumptions, and the priorities you will not trade away.
- **What is a development intent brief?** A short structured document that says what you are trying to build, for whom, at what cost, and what matters most when something has to give.
- **How do I explain my project to a contractor or lender without drawings?** Numbers and priorities, in that order: unit count and mix, gross square footage, target cost per square foot, site constraints you know about, and the three things that decide the project for you.
- **What is a massing diagram?** A simple block representation of a building's volume, footprint and height on the site — no windows, no materials, no interior layout.

## Use it

- [Open BuildBrief](https://buildbrief.nesohq.com/)
